text: Sir Manuel Amadeo Esquivel KCMG, PC (2 May 1940 – 10 February 2022) was a Belizean politician who served as the second prime minister of Belize from 1984 to 1989 and again from 1993 to 1998. As leader of the United Democratic Party (UDP), his party's victory in the 1984 general election marked the first time an opposition party had won since universal suffrage was introduced in 1954. Born in Belize City, then the capital of the British Crown Colony of British Honduras, Esquivel attended St John's College and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in physics from Loyola University New Orleans. He later obtained a postgraduate certificate in physics education from Bristol University, England. After the 1969 British Honduras election, he became head of the pro-business Liberal Party, which merged with two other parties in 1973 to form the UDP. He served two terms on the Belize City Council and was UDP chairman from 1976 to 1982. In the 1979 election, he ran for the Freetown constituency but was defeated by George Cadle Price of the People's United Party (PUP). He was then appointed a minority member of the Belize Senate, where he defeated Philip Goldson in January 1983 to become the first and only politician elected leader of a major Belizean political party while serving as a senator. Acting opposition leader Curl Thompson remained UDP's House leader until the next election. Esquivel was elected to the House of Representatives in December 1984 from the newly formed Caribbean Shores constituency, becoming prime minister shortly after. He held the seat until the 1998 election, when he was defeated by Jose Coye of the PUP. During his first term, the Price government faced a financial crisis and entered a standby agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) after raising tax rates twice. Upon becoming prime minister, Esquivel implemented economic reforms advised by domestic experts such as Edney Cain, shifting Belize's economy away from a mixed model toward increased foreign direct investment and tourism growth. In his second term, he introduced unpopular austerity measures, including suspending public sector pay raises from 1995 to 1997, while transferring 450,000 shares of Belize Telecommunications to a trust for affected workers. The opposition PUP labeled him "VATMAN" for introducing a 15% value-added tax (VAT) in 1995; the VAT was repealed by his successor Said Musa in 1999, who later introduced a 10% goods and services tax (GST) in 2005. After the UDP won the February 2008 election, Esquivel was appointed senior advisor to government with the rank of minister by Prime Minister Dean Barrow on 12 February 2008. He was also appointed Chairman of the Central Bank of Belize on 18 January 2011, stepping down in September 2013 and resigning from the Cabinet in March 2014. Post-retirement, Esquivel continued to offer public commentary, advocating for a standardized definition of the national flag and coat of arms, supporting decriminalization of small amounts of cannabis in 2017, and publishing an editorial in the Amandala newspaper in support of the 2019 Belizean territorial dispute referendum. He and his wife were among the first citizens to receive the COVID-19 vaccine for those over 60 when the government began administering it. Esquivel met his future wife, Kathleen Levy, while studying in Bristol; they married in 1971 and had three children: David, Laura, and Ruth. Laura served as a Belize City councilor (2006–2012), Director of the Belize Tourism Board (2012–2014), and Deputy Chief of Mission at the Embassy of Belize in Washington, D.C. He was involved in two vehicle rollovers on the Western Highway in 1996 and 2009 due to wet road conditions; the first caused only minor injuries, while the second required facial surgery. Kathleen, Lady Esquivel, authored a biography titled *Still Waters*, published in 2021. Esquivel died on 10 February 2022 at the age of 81. He was appointed to the Privy Council of the United Kingdom by Queen Elizabeth II in 1986, earning the title "Right Honourable," and received an Honorary Doctorate of Humane Letters from Loyola University. He was appointed Knight Commander of the Order of St Michael and St George (KCMG) in the 2010 New Year Honours. In 2021, the Belize City Council renamed an overpass and the coastal road connecting Belize District and Stann Creek District after him.
